# Custom resources

<!-- Generated by `go run ./internal/gendocs`: edit the source it names, not this file. -->

_Generated from the types in [`controller/api`](../../controller/api), through controller-gen's CRDs._

What the maxcloud controller works from. The app registry creates Buckets, Databases and Domains from an app's entry (apps can read them, not change them); apps may create DatabaseBranches. `kubectl get maxcloud -n <app>` lists them all. How the controller acts on them: [controller/README.md](../../controller/README.md).

- [Bucket](#bucket)
- [Database](#database)
- [DatabaseBranch](#databasebranch)
- [Domain](#domain)

## Bucket

`apiVersion: maxcloud.gronblom.dev/v1alpha1`, `kubectl get buckets`

Bucket is an S3 bucket for an app on the run platform. The app registry
creates these; apps can only read them.

The name becomes part of the bucket's: lowercase letters, digits and
single hyphens (no "--", which separates app and bucket), and not "db",
which is the app's database backups.

### spec

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `public` | boolean |  | Public lets anyone read the bucket's objects without credentials (s3:GetObject for everyone). Listing and writing still need the app's credentials. If the cluster gives public buckets hostnames, the bucket is also served at status.url. |
| `reclaimPolicy` | string: Retain, Delete | `Retain` | ReclaimPolicy: Retain (default) keeps the bucket and its objects when this object is deleted; Delete deletes them. |

### status

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bucketName` | string |  | BucketName is the bucket's name in Object Storage. |
| `conditions` | list of conditions |  | Conditions: Ready. When it's False, its reason is NotATenant (the namespace isn't an app's), InvalidName or APIError, and its message says why. |
| `endpoint` | string |  | Endpoint is the S3 endpoint the bucket is reached at. |
| `objects` | integer (int64) |  | Objects is the number of objects in the bucket, from UpCloud's bucket metrics, refreshed every few minutes. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | ObservedGeneration is the spec generation the conditions describe. |
| `sizeBytes` | integer (int64) |  | SizeBytes is the bytes stored in the bucket, from UpCloud's bucket metrics, refreshed every few minutes. |
| `url` | string |  | URL a public bucket's objects are served at (behind the CDN), when the cluster gives public buckets hostnames. |

## Database

`apiVersion: maxcloud.gronblom.dev/v1alpha1`, `kubectl get databases`

Database is a Postgres database for an app on the run platform. The app
registry creates it; apps can only read it.

One database per app for now: its Cluster is db, its backups mc-&lt;app&gt;--db.

### spec

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `backup` | object |  | Backup settings: when base backups are taken and how long backups are kept. |
| `backup.retention` | string | `7d` | Retention of backups and WAL: a number of days, weeks or months (7d, 2w, 1m). It's how far back a restore can go. |
| `backup.schedule` | string | `0 0 5 * * *` | Schedule of the base backups, CloudNativePG's six-field cron (seconds first); the default is daily at 05:00. WAL is archived continuously in between, at least every 5 minutes. Each new backup generation also gets a base backup of its own as soon as its Cluster is ready. |
| `instances` | integer (int32) | `1` | Instances: 1, or 2 for a streaming replica (on another node when CloudNativePG can place it there), so a node drain fails over instead of taking the database down. With 2 the Cluster gets a PodDisruptionBudget; with 1 it doesn't, so it never blocks a drain. |
| `reclaimPolicy` | string: Retain, Delete | `Retain` | ReclaimPolicy of the backup bucket mc-&lt;app&gt;--db: Retain (default) keeps the backups when this object is deleted; Delete deletes the bucket and every backup in it. |
| `resources` | object |  | Resources of each Postgres instance (default: 20m CPU and 128Mi memory requested, 512Mi memory limit). Set, it replaces the default as a whole; only requests and limits are used. |
| `resources.claims` | list |  | Claims lists the names of resources, defined in spec.resourceClaims, that are used by this container.<br><br>This field depends on the DynamicResourceAllocation feature gate.<br><br>This field is immutable. It can only be set for containers. |
| `resources.claims[].name` | string, required |  | Name must match the name of one entry in pod.spec.resourceClaims of the Pod where this field is used. It makes that resource available inside a container. |
| `resources.claims[].request` | string |  | Request is the name chosen for a request in the referenced claim. If empty, everything from the claim is made available, otherwise only the result of this request. |
| `resources.limits` | object |  | Limits describes the maximum amount of compute resources allowed. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `resources.requests` | object |  | Requests describes the minimum amount of compute resources required. If Requests is omitted for a container, it defaults to Limits if that is explicitly specified, otherwise to an implementation-defined value. Requests cannot exceed Limits. More info: https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/configuration/manage-resources-containers/ |
| `size` |  | `1Gi` | Size of each instance's disk. It can grow (the disks are resized in place), never shrink: a smaller value than the Cluster has is ignored. |

### status

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `bucket` | string |  | Bucket holding the backups (mc-&lt;app&gt;--db). |
| `conditions` | list of conditions |  | Conditions: Ready; Blocked (True while the controller won't act until a person decides, with why in its message); Restore (the last restore: True with reason Restored, or False with reason Refused when a restore-to time couldn't be used). |
| `generation` | integer (int64) |  | Generation of the backups the database writes now: they go to the folder db-&lt;generation&gt; in the bucket. A restore starts a new one, so older backups are never written over. The bucket's marker (maxcloud.json) is the source of truth; this is a copy. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | ObservedGeneration is the spec generation the conditions describe. |
| `phase` | string |  | Phase is where the database is: Creating, Restoring, Ready or Blocked. |
| `restoredFrom` | integer (int64) |  | RestoredFrom is the generation the current one was restored from; unset for a database that started empty. |
| `restoredTo` | string (date-time) |  | RestoredTo is the point in time the current generation was restored to, if it was (restore-to). |

## DatabaseBranch

`apiVersion: maxcloud.gronblom.dev/v1alpha1`, `kubectl get databasebranches`

DatabaseBranch is a throwaway copy of an app's database. Unlike Database
and Bucket, apps make these themselves (mcloud db branch): it counts
against the app's quota, and deleting it deletes the copy.

### spec

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `at` | string (date-time) |  | At: the point in time to branch from (RFC 3339). Empty: the latest. It can't be before the end of the oldest finished base backup the database still has. |
| `database` | string | `db` | Database to branch, in the same namespace. It needs at least one finished base backup. |
| `size` |  |  | Size of the branch's disk (default: the database's spec.size). |

### status

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `cluster` | string |  | Cluster is the branch's CloudNativePG Cluster; its connection details are in the Secret &lt;Cluster&gt;-app (key uri). |
| `conditions` | list of conditions |  | Conditions: Ready. When the branch failed, its reason is one of NoDatabase, NoBackupBefore, ClusterGone, Blocked (a Cluster of that name that isn't the branch's) or NotATenant. |
| `fromGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | FromGeneration is the database's backup generation it was restored from. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | ObservedGeneration is the spec generation the conditions describe. |
| `phase` | string |  | Phase is where the branch is: Creating, Ready or Failed. |

## Domain

`apiVersion: maxcloud.gronblom.dev/v1alpha1`, `kubectl get domains`

Domain is a custom hostname for one of an app's Knative services. The
app registry creates these from the app's entry (domains), within the
hostnames an admin allowed the app; apps can only read them.

The name is the hostname: lowercase DNS labels, at least two of them.

### spec

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `proxied` | boolean |  | Proxied puts the hostname behind Cloudflare (its DNS record is proxied, through external-dns's cloudflare-proxied annotation on the route): WAF, caching, Cloudflare Access. Cloudflare's free edge certificate only covers names one level below the zone. |
| `service` | string, required |  | Service is the Knative service in this namespace (for a function, the function's name). Until Knative has a route for it, the Domain isn't Ready (ServiceNotFound). |

### status

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `conditions` | list of conditions |  | Conditions: Ready. When it's False, the hostname isn't routed, and the reason is NotAllowed (not on the admin's allowlist for the app), NoListener (no HTTPS listener covers it), ServiceNotFound (Knative has no route for the service), HostInUse (another HTTPRoute on the Gateway has the hostname; checked again every minute) or NotATenant. |
| `listener` | string |  | Listener is the Gateway listener (and so the certificate) serving the hostname: the HTTPS listener for exactly that name, else the longest wildcard that covers it one level deep. |
| `observedGeneration` | integer (int64) |  | ObservedGeneration is the spec generation the conditions describe. |
| `revisions` | list |  | Revisions the hostname currently sends requests to, as Knative's own route for the service does. |
| `url` | string |  | URL the service is reached at on this hostname. Empty while the Domain isn't Ready. |
